A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D3 research. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. v1 Appendices A-D correspond to v2 Appendices A-D; v2 adds Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments, scaling comparisons, robustness tests and ablations on merged UFD/GenImage data, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an occlusion-map comparison of D3 and UFD in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Both versions use frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 features from original and patch-shuffled images, self-attention fusion, a linear classifier and binary cross-entropy training. The diagram's broader 'Feature Extractor' label does not establish an architecture change.

E1.justification: Both use the same merged UFD/GenImage coverage: eight training generators and twelve unseen generators. The new occlusion analysis does not establish an additional dataset, domain or detection task.

E2.justification: The evaluated baseline set remains CNNDet, Patchfor, LNP, DIRE and UFD. UFD remains the qualitative comparator and is reused in the new occlusion analysis.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the stated single-generator training example involving ProGAN with ADM, retaining Midjourney as the other condition. Appendix E introduces occlusion-based inference probing. Main benchmark splits, metrics, preprocessing and training budgets remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish benchmark reruns.

E4.justification: New Appendix E and supplementary Figure 2 compare occlusion maps for six fake images correctly detected by D3 but missed by UFD. Existing component ablations, disruption comparisons, robustness tests, patch-size sensitivity and classifier-head studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average scaling results over three random generator orders in Section 4.4 and Figure 2. No new run counts, seed disclosures, confidence intervals or statistical estimation practices are introduced.

E6.justification: All six corresponding numerical tables and existing performance plots are unchanged. Section 3.1 replaces the ProGAN/87.6% example with ADM/83.2%, retaining Midjourney/58.9%; these are different stated training conditions. Appendix E adds qualitative occlusion findings. v2 also newly claims Patchfor initially trails CNNDet, although retained Figure 2 shows it slightly ahead.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, feature-extraction equations and classification loss retain their mathematical content. Renaming PatchShuffle to PS and the batch-size symbol does not change the mathematics. No new theorem, proof or formal assumption appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add detector-performance divergence during scaling as an explicit contribution, claiming that multi-generator generalization imposes different requirements. The central D3 proposal and claimed 5.3-percentage-point OOD advantage remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 expands the interpretation of divergent scaling behavior and interprets broader occlusion responses as evidence of more comprehensive, universal artifacts. Appendix E attributes UFD mistakes to narrow attention. The limitations concerning doubled backbone computation and dataset adequacy are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub pointer promising source-code updates. Section 4.3 removes specific baseline details, including LNP preprocessing and DIRE's 256x256 unconditional diffusion model. D3 training hyperparameters and appendix classifier configurations remain documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zeiler and Fergus's visualization work and removes the distinct Gragnaniello et al. and Sohl-Dickstein et al. references. Related-work discussion is shortened, and CLIP-based detection is reframed as pretrained-based detection; the overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: v2 revises portions of the abstract, introduction and contribution list, compresses related-work and baseline descriptions, and updates terminology and author information. It adds acknowledgements and corrects the conclusion's 'train-on-one' wording to 'train-on-many'. Most section order and exposition are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column presentation, extensively relocating and resizing figures and tables and introducing separate supplementary numbering. Appendix tables move closer to their discussion, the framework diagram is relabeled, and a new six-case occlusion-map figure is added.

improvement.justification: The new occlusion case study and closer placement of appendix tables improve explanation and navigation. However, v2 removes concrete baseline implementation details and adds an initial Patchfor-versus-CNNDet ranking claim inconsistent with retained Figure 2. With the central method and quantitative evidence unchanged, these competing benefits and regressions do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
